source_title: Blind date: ‘He said: “If heaven is real, you’ll definitely be going there”, which might be the nicest thing anyone’s ever said to me’
source_excerpt:
Nelson, 41, who works in legal services, meets Louise, 37, who works in marketing
What were you hoping for? Great company and wonderful conversation.
First impressions? Louise is such a sweet, sincere person. With very interesting hobbies!
What did you talk about? All sorts of funny things, from feeding monkeys to the worst theatre shows and wooden toys.
Most awkward moment? When we met, I wanted to greet her with a friendly hug but she was seated and had to get up.
Good table manners? Impeccable, and she had amazing taco-eating skills.
Best thing about Louise? She will laugh and think I’m taking the mick but I’m not: her dedication to the things she loves. So admirable! Passion and commitment. It’s infectious.
Would you introduce Louise to your friends? Yes.
Blind date is Saturday’s dating column: every week, two strangers are paired up for dinner and drinks, and then spill the beans to us, answering a set of questions. This runs, with a photograph we take of each dater before the date, in Saturday magazine (in the UK) and online at theguardian.com every Saturday. It’s been running since 2009 – you can read all about how we put it together here . What questions will I be asked? We ask about age, location, occupation, hobbies, interests and the type of person you are looking to meet. If you do not think these questions cover everything you would like to know, tell us what’s on your mind.
Can I choose who I match with? No, it’s a blind date! But we do ask you a bit about your interests, preferences, etc – the more you tell us, the better the match is likely to be.
Can I pick the photograph? No, but don't worry: we'll choose the nicest ones.
What personal details will appear? Your first name, job and age.
How should I answer? Honestly but respectfully. Be mindful of how it will read to your date, and that Blind date reaches a large audience, in print and online.
Will I see the other person’s answers? No. We may edit yours and theirs for a range of reasons, including length, and we may ask you for more details.
Will you find me The One? We’ll try! Marriage! Babies!
Can I do it in my home town? Only if it’s in the UK. Many of our applicants live in London, but we would love to hear from people living elsewhere.
How to apply Email blind.date@theguardian.com
Describe Louise in three words Energetic, passionate, excellent conversationalist (four I know!).
What do you think Louise made of you? An oddball with similar interests?
Did you go on somewhere? It was a work night so we remained sensible.
If you could change one thing about the date, what would it be? I wouldn’t change a thing! It was a very pleasant date overall.
Marks out of 10? 9 out of 10. A really pleasant evening!
What were you hoping for? Fun conversation with an interesting person and to discover a new restaurant.
First impressions? A gentleman, very polite, laughs very loudly (in a good way).
What did you talk about? London zoo volunteering – a typical day. Nelson growing up in Singapore. Covid – how I was in Singapore and Bali just as it started kicking off. Theatre shows we’ve been to – how perfect Oliver! is (this was mainly me). How we both go and see all the Oscar-nominated films every awards season. Nelson’s new startup.
Most awkward moment? The waitress thought a photographer would be joining us and we needed a table for three.
Good table manners? I was more conscious of my own, as I ate the tacos with my hands while he used cutlery.
Best thing about Nelson? He’s a very interesting and interested person – so many hobbies and passions. I liked that he shared my enthusiasm for all things cultural.
Would you introduce Nelson to your friends? Can’t think why not, he’s very interesting and sweet!
Describe Nelson in three words Perceptive, warm, bright.
What do you think Nelson made of you? He said: “If heaven is real, you’ll definitely be going there”, which might just be the nicest thing anyone’s ever said to me. He also laughed very heartily all the way through so hopefully he thought I was funny.
Did you go on somewhere? No, but we were the last to leave on a Tuesday night, so pretty good going.
If you could change one thing about the evening, what would it be? The pineapple/lime/cinnamon ice-cream was incredible, we should’ve got one each.
Marks out of 10? 8 (the date, not Nelson as a person!).
Would you meet again? I think as friends – maybe at the cinema as Oscar season is approaching!
Nelson and Louise ate at Mirtala , London W4. Fancy a blind date? Email blind.date@theguardian.com
